name: Tana Outliner
tagline: A node-based outliner with supertags, fields, and live queries that turns notes into a queryable graph.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The outliner part is a solved problem: nested nodes, keyboard-driven indent and collapse, backlinks, and a local store are all well-trodden ground for a coding agent. Where it gets hard is the thing Tana is actually about: supertags that attach schemas to nodes, fields that behave like database columns, and live queries that re-render as the graph changes. You can get a credible single-user version of that in a weekend if you accept a simpler query language and no real-time sync. What you will not get in one sitting is the mobile capture app, the voice-to-structured-node pipeline, multiplayer editing, or the performance work that keeps a graph of 100k nodes from stuttering. Call it a good personal outliner with database pretensions, not a Tana replacement.
coreLoopDIY: A local-first outliner where any node can be tagged with a schema that adds typed fields, plus saved queries that list matching nodes live.
requirements: Local storage or SQLite for persistence
Patience for keyboard-handling edge cases in contenteditable
whatYouLose: Mobile capture, including voice notes that arrive as structured nodes
The AI features that fill fields and generate nodes from prose
Performance and undo behavior on very large graphs
Calendar, day-node, and integration plumbing you would have to hand-roll
moatNotes: The moat is not the network, it is the editor. Outliner keyboard behavior, undo, and query performance take years of unglamorous work, and once your graph lives there, moving it out is genuinely painful.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because outliners live or die on feel, and feel is the part nobody one-shots. Tana's value shows up in the thousand small interactions: how indent behaves at the edge of a list, how a query updates when you change a field, how fast the thing is when your graph is huge. A weekend build gives you the concept and none of the muscle memory, and a personal knowledge base is exactly the kind of tool where friction makes you stop using it. Also, your notes accumulate, and the accumulated graph is the thing you are really paying to keep working.
notes: The concept is a weekend; the editor feel is not.
prompt:
Build a local-first, single-user networked outliner in an empty folder. Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- Zustand for state
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 in a tiny Express server, or Dexie/IndexedDB if you prefer zero backend: pick ONE and commit
- No auth, no cloud, no telemetry, no accounts

Data model:
- Node: id, parentId, order (fractional index), content (plain text with inline [[links]]), collapsed, createdAt, updatedAt
- Tag (call it a supertag): id, name, fieldDefs: array of { key, type: text | number | date | nodeRef | checkbox }
- NodeTag: nodeId, tagId, values: record of fieldKey to value

Editor requirements:
- One infinite outline, bullet per node, contenteditable or textarea per node, your call
- Keyboard: Enter creates a sibling, Tab indents, Shift+Tab outdents, Backspace at start merges up, Up/Down move caret across nodes, Cmd+Shift+Up/Down reorder siblings, Cmd+. toggles collapse
- Typing # opens a tag picker; selecting a tag attaches it and renders its fields inline under the node
- Typing [[ opens a node picker; selecting creates a reference link
- Clicking a bullet zooms into that node as the new root, with breadcrumbs
- Backlinks panel listing nodes that reference the current node

Queries:
- A node whose content starts with QUERY: is a live query node
- Support a deliberately simple syntax: tag:project status:active sort:updatedAt
- Render matching nodes as a live child list that updates when the store changes

Also include:
- Full-text search box with fuzzy-ish matching, Cmd+K to open
- Export and import the whole graph as JSON
- Undo/redo for node edits and structural moves (at least 50 steps)

Explicitly out of scope: sync, multiplayer, mobile app, AI anything, sharing, publishing, plugins.

Deliver a README with run instructions and a seed script that loads ~200 demo nodes so performance is visible. Keep any secrets in .env, though this build should need none.
